recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not edit the inactive request-stage files for FHIR-11127; any cleanup of those stale files should be handled separately from this already-applied request-intent resolution.
issue_request: FHIR-11127 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU2 request about required DiagnosticRequest.stage forcing systems to choose original-order or reflex-order when they only knew the request was an order. The approved resolution was to define a generic order code rather than make the modifier element optional.
initial_application: Commit 135effcdc18c5860253e8fc6df7197732441fe74 explicitly mentioned FHIR-11127 and changed DiagnosticRequest.stage to DiagnosticRequest.intent with a required request-intent binding. Later request-pattern work replaced DiagnosticRequest and DeviceUseRequest with current ServiceRequest and DeviceRequest surfaces and centralized the RequestIntent code system.
additional_context: Related Published decisions FHIR-11190 and FHIR-12052 renamed stage to intent and kept the concept required while allowing detailed order-like codes to map under order. Current fhir.ini lists ServiceRequest and DeviceRequest as active resources. The old request-stage XML files remain in source but are not active fhir.ini codesystem/value set entries and are not the binding used by the current request resources.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. ServiceRequest.intent and DeviceRequest.intent remain 1..1 modifier elements bound to ValueSet/request-intent, and source/request/codesystem-request-intent.xml includes order with original-order, reflex-order, filler-order, and instance-order descendants.

related_jiras.note: Published decision that renamed DiagnosticRequest.stage to intent and pointed to the same order-mapping concept.
